subject: Post-demo recap: latency targets, throughput, and data sovereignty checks
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintextlabs.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 8 Feb 2027 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: latency targets, throughput, and data sovereignty checks

Hi Sarah — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and asks so we can align the perf qualification timeline:

1) Latency targets
- Your primary SLO: 95th percentile tail <= 120ms for single-turn text generation at 512 tokens (avg prompt + 64 token completion).
- Secondary: streaming use-case for live transcription must keep first-byte latency < 300ms for 1s segments.

2) Throughput & concurrency
- Peak concurrency estimate you shared: 550 concurrent sessions, average QPS ~180 during peak 30-minute windows.
- We need confirmation of session distribution (steady vs. spiky) and whether bursts exceed 1k QPS.

3) Regional routing & data residency
- You asked for primary serving from us-east-1 with EU fallback (eu-west-1) and APAC read-only replica (ap-southeast-1) for lower-latency reads.
- Data sovereignty: customer PII must remain in EU for EU-based users; logs/metrics can be aggregated in US but raw transcript storage must be EU-only.

Next steps I propose:
- FinText: confirm burst profile (CSV sample of per-minute QPS across a typical day).
- FinText: flag which user cohorts are EU-only for residency enforcement.
- Redwood: deliver an SLO matrix and a suggested routing topology (attached) by EOD tomorrow.

Attachments: redwood-slo-matrix-v1.xlsx (SLO assumptions), regional-routing-diagram.png (initial routing sketch).

If that matches your expectations I can spin up a short pilot config and share a targeted runbook for qualification.

Thanks,
Connor
Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime and tooling

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintextlabs.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@fintextlabs.com, Dana Park <legal@fintextlabs.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Feb 2027 09:01:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: latency targets, throughput, and data sovereignty checks

Thanks Connor — great demo. Quick notes and clarifications:

- Latency: 95p <= 120ms at 512 tokens is our aspirational target. For rollout we can accept a staged SLO: 95p <= 180ms for the pilot, with goal to tune to 120ms in production.
- Streaming: live transcription is mission-critical for certain enterprise accounts (approx 10% of sessions). First-byte < 300ms requirement is correct.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent sessions were estimated ~550, but that includes internal testing traffic. Real-world peak likely 420-480; however during earnings days we have unpredictable spike behavior, potentially 900+ for 5–10 minute windows.

On data residency:
- EU users (about 22% of active base) must have transcripts stored and processed in EU. For analytics/aggregates, anonymized metrics can be replicated to US.
- We will provide a list of EU-only user cohorts by EOD Wednesday (10 Feb).

I attached our sample traffic CSV (anonymized) to this reply. Also, procurement asked for a short note on what evidence we need to validate EU residency (SOC2 logs? KMS proofs?). Dana (legal) will loop in specific contract phrasing.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Kim
Head of Product, FinText Labs
sarah.kim@fintextlabs.com

Attachments: fintxt-traffic-sample-agg.csv

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@fintextlabs.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 08:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: latency targets, throughput, and data sovereignty checks

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Sarah. Confirming receipt of the traffic sample — that helps a lot. A few follow-ups after we reviewed the CSV: 

- Burst handling: we can simulate the 900+ spikes in a short pilot run (50m window) but we recommend a short warm-up window and autoscaler headroom set to 2.2x observed peak to avoid cold-start tail latency during bursts.
- Streaming path: we'll validate first-byte latency in the pilot with a 95th percentile target of < 300ms; if we can't meet that with standard batch settings we'll propose a dedicated streaming config that sacrifices some throughput for lower initial latency.
- EU residency: for strict compliance we'll offer an option to restrict both processing and at-rest transcript storage to eu-west-1. That will require a per-customer tenancy flag and separate KMS for EU keys.

I've attached an updated SLO matrix (redwood-slo-matrix-v1.xlsx) with pilot vs. production targets and a routing diagram showing the EU data-only path (ttl-data-residency-note.pdf explains the KMS options).

Action items: 
- FinText (Sarah): confirm which 3 enterprise customers need EU-only tenancy for pilot.
- FinText (procurement): share required evidence checklist for residency (SOC2 snippets, proof-of-key-location).
- Redwood (Vanessa): prepare pilot infra estimate and a preliminary committed throughput quote; copy me and Aditya.

I'll wait for the EU cohort list and procurement requests and then propose dates for a 2-week pilot starting late Feb.

Thanks,
Connor

--

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: latency targets, throughput, and data sovereignty checks

Hi Sarah — looping in procurement/ops context. Two quick notes from my side: 

1) Pilot estimate and pricing shape:
- For a 2-week pilot that simulates 1x baseline + 2.2x headroom for burst testing across US/EU, ballpark: $12,500 for reserved pilot capacity (includes monitoring, prioritized routing).
- If you want EU-only tenancy for specific customers, there will be an add-on for dedicated KMS & separate storage nodes (~+25% on pilot infra).

2) Evidence for residency/proof points (what Redwood can provide):
- KMS key location/current key IDs (we can provide signed attestations).
- Object storage bucket region listing and signed access logs for the pilot period.
- Audit log extracts showing processing region for a sample session.

Connor will coordinate technical runbook. Happy to set up a short procurement call Thursday to align contract checklist.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
